scope: Core owned input handle cleanup versus terminal adapter reacquisition regression tests

redReasons: Terminal abort leaves previously acquired original input unclosed
Normal body-read completion reacquires adapter handle instead of reusing original

assessment: GuardedExchange reuses existing lifecycle fixture and returns a real counted InputStream; after transport abort its requestBody accessor explicitly rejects a recycled container. The application positively decodes exact original bytes before abort, establishing an owned handle whose close is required independently of later accessor availability.

Abort case requires original input close1 and total adapter access1, followed by late Deferred settlement/repeated abort still close1. It therefore distinguishes a leak, reacquisition and duplicate cleanup.
Normal-read case requires exact echoed original payload, close1 and getter1, preventing a fix limited to exception suppression or cancellation only.

Unread normal positive checks getter0 while callback runs, input still open after send within the active callback, then one lazy getter/close after unwind. This protects no-eager-acquisition and active ownership.
Preserved actual RED reaches the intended two cleanup assertions while the unread control passes. Only one new test class changes; no production/dependency/test weakening.
limitations: Production input-cache synchronization and full body/abort/retention regressions still require GREEN/source review. Existing actual Servlet fallback tests provide complementary real-container evidence.
actions: Read-only pinned test/evidence review; no edits/builds/network. Wrote tmp report only; first PASS ends loop.
